summary: The documented 64 MiB durable-root bound is now real across restarts and Sessions (Issue #89). RlmRuntimeImpl rescans durableRoot at construction into a byte accounting map (v2 envelopes + legacy v1 pairs counted by file size, stale .tmp- owners removed), publishDurable charges only the delta against the persisted aggregate and skips over-quota candidates non-fatally (previous valid generation kept, recovery.durable={published:false,reason} surfaced without failing the user cell), snapshotFor reservation now counts durable bytes plus reservations of sessions without a durable generation (no double counting), and reset releases the Session share via dropDurable.

pointers: Issue#89 quota enforced across sessions and restart

steps: Verified at 5a1b6e1: checkpointReservations was an in-memory map only, so a new runtime over the same durableRoot started from an empty budget while old files remained.
Unified accounting keys on the SHA-256 file name (rescan derives them from file names; publish/drop used the raw sessionKey before the fix, double-counting after restart).

Regression fills 8 sessions x 7.5 MiB (payload cap 8 MiB), proves the ninth is bounded and non-fatal, a same-Session zero-delta replacement still publishes while the root is full, a NEW runtime sees the persisted bytes, and reset releases its share so new publication is admitted.

evidence.note: ~3s runtime with 8 real 7.5 MiB checkpoints on Windows

limitations: Accounting is size-based: validity is enforced at read time, and hosts sharing one durableRoot race at publication time (admission is per-process best-effort).
